label: rem:lepton-number-categorical-properties
title: Conservation, $\mathbb{Z}$-grading, and the $\chi = -6$ constraint on lepton number
html:
The categorical lepton number possesses several structural properties.

Each beta decay applies the Skein relation at one crossing. This produces a smoothing L_0^{\pm}. It contains exactly one lepton–antilepton pair. Lepton number counts these smoothings.

Each smoothing L_0^{\pm} contributes:

  • One charged lepton (e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 or e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}) with lepton number \pm 1.
  • One neutrino or antineutrino (K_{0_1} or K_{0_1}^{\sigma}) with lepton number -1.

The net lepton number of each L_0^{\pm} pair is zero.

Conservation. Lepton number is conserved by construction:

  1. Skein smoothings produce lepton pairs with net lepton number 0. The nuclear sector loses one crossing. Hadrons carry lepton number 0. The total is \Delta L = 0.
  2. Gröbner–Shirshov re-reduction acts within the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. It produces no smoothings. The total is \Delta L = 0.
  3. Markov moves change the braid representative but not the link type. The total is \Delta L = 0.

Every process expressed as a sequence of Skein relations and Hecke reductions conserves lepton number.

Lepton number is not a \mathbb{Z}-grading (proved). The Skein module \mathcal{K}(S^3; q) admits no \mathbb{Z}-grading by the smoothing count with the nuclear sector in grade 0 and each smoothing shifting the grade by +1.

The skein relation is inhomogeneous for such a grading. Writing it as

  L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0 ,

the left-hand side is a difference of grade-g classes, hence grade g, while the right-hand side carries one further smoothing, hence grade g+1 (scalars are grade-preserving). An element lying in two distinct homogeneous components is 0, so the relation forces (q - q^{-1})L_0 = 0 and L_+ = L_-. Imposing the grading therefore annihilates every smoothing: it would make lepton number identically 0, which is the one value it cannot take.

This is a scope-(b) exclusion of one construction, with its invariant cited (the defining disjointness of homogeneous components); it does not touch lepton number itself, the Skein module, or the Y = B - L route.

What this leaves, and where L does live. An inhomogeneous relation is what a filtration tolerates rather than a grading, but the Vassiliev filtration grades invariants v : K \to R, not states, so it does not by itself supply a state-valued L.

The carrier is the braid word, not the knot type. This is forced: L cannot factor through the unframed knot type, since the mirror must move the carrier and the unknot is amphichiral. It is also the convention of Antiparticles from crossing reversal, which takes the mirror to be \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} on braid words and records that it preserves the knot type.

The braid words are \nu_e = \sigma_1 and, by the electron ruling (electron), e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, with antiparticles \sigma_1^{-1} and \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} --- distinct braid words (the neutrino words close to the unknot, the electron words to the positive and negative Hopf links), which is exactly how the mirror acts freely. Both electron words have writhe \pm 3, as \sigma_1^{\pm 3} did, so the signs below are unchanged. The writhes follow from the words, and the candidate

  L(\beta) = \mathrm{sign}\bigl(\mathrm{writhe}(\beta)\bigr)

reproduces every row of the table below, hadrons included. It is a candidate, not a derivation: \mathrm{sign} is a choice of function, the quark braid word is still absent from the corpus, and chirality (u_L vs u_R) is not yet represented.

And it is refuted, under both readings of the gauge freedom.

Markov II. Stabilisation raises the writhe by 1 without changing the link, so L jumps from 0 to 1 on the baryon --- violating conservation clause 3 above, which requires \Delta L = 0 under Markov moves .

The minimal-level ruling. The escape from the first refutation was that states are Gröbner--Shirshov normal forms, with the observable evaluated at the lowest level of the substrate tower. That closes the escape rather than opening it. The table above assigns \nu_e = K_{0_1} = T_{2,1}, the unknot, whose braid index is 1: its minimal-level normal form is the empty word, and so is its mirror's. At the level where the framework says observables live, \nu_e and \nu_e^{\sigma} are the same state, and no function of the state can give them +1 and -1 --- quite apart from \mathrm{sign}(0) = 0 \neq +1. This is proved, and it is the same obstruction established above for the unframed knot type, reappearing once the canonical representative is pinned.

So the "carrier is the braid word, not the knot type" escape is unavailable at minimal level, where the braid word is determined by the knot type. Scope-(a): L = \mathrm{sign}(w) is refuted; lepton number itself and the Y = B - L route are untouched, and what the refutation locates is that L must come from data the writhe does not carry --- the framing or the smoothing history, not the crossing sum.

Individual lepton assignments.

Particle Knot type Lepton number L Origin
e^- \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (closure: Hopf link) +1 L_0^{-} charged component (\beta^-)
e^+ \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} (closure: negative Hopf link) -1 L_0^{+} charged component (\beta^+)
\nu_e K_{0_1} (unknot) +1 L_0^{+} neutral component (\beta^+)
\nu_e^{\sigma} K_{0_1}^{\sigma} (mirror unknot) -1 L_0^{-} neutral component (\beta^-)

The charged lepton carries L = \pm 1. The neutrino carries L = \mp 1. Each pair sums to zero.

The \chi = -6 constraint. In the Descartes universe, the Euler characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 constrains Bring's surface. The torus knot generators T(2, n) with odd n \leq 7 exhaust the fermion spectrum. In the backup model the electron (T_{2,3}) and neutrino (K_{0_1} = T_{2,1}) are the lowest torus knots in this sequence, and the argument read the smoothing L_0^{-} as decomposing into exactly these single-component closures. This selection does not hold for the ruled electron. The closure of \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is the Hopf link, which has two components and is not a T(2,n) with odd n. So the \chi = -6 constraint, as stated, does not select the electron. Scope-(a): this is a statement about this argument, not about lepton number, whose conservation clauses above do not use it.

Structural origin of lepton-number conservation. In the Standard Model, lepton number conservation is an accidental symmetry. Here, it is a structural invariant. The Skein relation is the unique operation that changes crossing type. It always produces exactly one lepton pair. The Iwahori–Hecke algebra contains no mechanism to produce an odd number of leptons. The smoothing is a topological operation on a single crossing. Each smoothing is binary.

Lepton number violation requires a process that changes crossing type without passing through the Skein relation. Such a process must exist outside the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. In the \chi = -6 universe, no such process exists.
